probe: When this spec is done, what exists that doesn't exist now - a written system design you can read and act on, or working software? Is the finish line a document you approve, or a thing that is running?
response: let's clearly define the business and execution, then the architecture stack and build it

probe: Which pain is real - lost hours (efficiency, competes with ops consultants) or I am behind on AI and have nobody local to ask (certainty, no competition)? Or a third one?
response: It is not you are losing hours, it is you are getting your time back. What would you do with 5-10 more hours every week? Spend more time selling, more time with your family, more time on R&D? It is an investment in getting your life back

probe: Is the buyer specifically the owner-operator personally in the machine (5-30 people), with bigger companies out of scope - or do you want a second version for larger shops where the pitch is money not time?
response: if we can bifurcate it and speak to ROI for bigger companies and FTE savings and efficiency vs the small business owner doing the work themselves and then bifurcate the marketing, perfect

probe: How do you want to position against the local competition - as the builder, as the guarantor, or both?
response: Competitive research validated: Slade and Lithium are SEO/web agencies doing automation as a sideline with no-code glue. Lumeor is national template pages. Local custom shops (SingleMind 150/hr 25-50k min, Uptech 50k+ min, Buildfire 149/hr 10-25k min) floor above the 10-30k band. Riverbend sells fractional COO systems-that-scale to 3-15M service businesses. Nobody offers a guarantee. Proof point: traditional dev shop quoted Loominary 300k where Russ offered 30k plus JV. Russ wants full business model, then architecture, then execution.

probe: Does the audit need boots on the ground, or can the bulk run remote with one on-site visit? Capacity determines whether this is a business or a job.
What does the guarantee become for the bigger track, and how is the audit priced per track?
response: Maybe make the fee based on headcount and tie fee to company size. Resolved as: 100 dollars per employee, 999 minimum, 15000 cap. Guarantee is 10x the fee in annual recoverable time or cost - expressed as hours-per-week for small owner-operators and as annual dollars for larger companies. Headcount is public so every list entry carries its own price pre-contact.
